key_insight: MM-Lifelong provides a natural, multimodal lifelog dataset (181.1 hours) organized at Day / Week / Month scales, exposing real-world temporal challenges and revealing that current MLLM paradigms break down on long-range, unscripted video.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between short, densely concatenated video benchmarks and real-world, unscripted daily lifelog footage by offering a temporally structured dataset and an agentic baseline to evaluate lifelong multimodal understanding.
method: Assemble MM-Lifelong: 181.1 hours of multimodal lifelog video organized into Day, Week, and Month temporal scales to capture varying event density and continuity.
Systematic evaluation of existing end-to-end MLLMs and retrieval-augmented approaches to identify two major failure modes in long-range temporal reasoning and memory retention.
Propose an agentic (modular) baseline that combines memory, retrieval, and action-oriented reasoning to better handle long-horizon multimodal understanding.
impact: Enables rigorous study of long-range temporal reasoning, memory, and continual understanding in multimodal systems, providing a benchmark and baseline that can accelerate development of models suited for real-world, unscripted lifelog applications.
visual_elements: Timeline infographic showing the Day / Week / Month dataset splits with total hours per scale and example frames
Heatmap or bar chart comparing temporal density (events/hour) across MM-Lifelong vs. standard video benchmarks
Schematic diagram of the agentic baseline (memory store + retrieval module + reasoning loop) contrasted with an end-to-end MLLM
Failure-mode panel: two illustrated failure cases (e.g., loss of long-range context, incorrect retrieval/memory overwriting) with brief captions
paper_title: Towards Multimodal Lifelong Understanding: A Dataset and Agentic Baseline
paper_authors: Guo Chen, Lidong Lu, Yicheng Liu, Liangrui Dong, Lidong Zou
